headline: Poet Laureate committee recommended a candidate; draft minutes from June 18, 2026 approved unanimously.
summary: The minutes cover library circulation, a temporary parking ban near the library, a delayed opening on September 18, and fountain bag sales. They also cover delays to the Brownstone Stairs project and an HVAC leak. The Trustees will consider a gift proposal for the library's fences.
decisions: Approved the draft minutes from June 18, 2026 unanimously.
The Poet Laureate Selection Committee recommended a candidate for the new Poet Laureate.

plain_text:
Draft of Minutes of Board of Trustees Meeting of September 17, 2026 
Salem, Massachusetts        September 17, 2026 
A meeting of the Board of Trustees was held via Zoom on this date at 4:10pm with Trustees 
April, Austin, Lutts, Rourke, and Trustee Buckley present and presiding. Mayor Pangallo and 
Trustee Morin were absent. Miss Mansfield was present. 
Approval of draft minutes from June 18, 2026 UNANIMOUS. 
John Hermanski addressed the Board and proposed a gift to address the issues with the library’s 
fences. The Trustees will consider the proposal. 
Current Library Use reports were distributed. Salem was fifth highest in NOBLE for circulation 
of physical items during June and July, and third highest in August. Salem was second highest in 
Overdrive/Libby circulation during June, July, and August. Miss Mansfield reported that the 
Temporary Resident Permit Parking ban went into effect on September 15th, which meant that 
patrons could no longer park on Essex Street on weekdays after 5pm or weekends after 12pm. 
Miss Mansfield reported that the library would have a delayed opening on Friday, September 
18th at 12:00pm due to staff training. She noted that the fall program session begins on Monday, 
September 21st and that adult yoga would return in November when evening parking is restored. 
Financial reports were distributed. Miss Mansfield reported that nine fountain bags were sold in 
September, and that an order had been placed to replenish the supply. Trustee Rourke suggested 
creating a printed QR code to put inside the bags that would allow people to learn more about the 
fountain’s history and how they can support the ongoing maintenance the fountain. 
Miss Mansfield reported that the Brownstone Stairs project was running behind schedule, but 
noted that the Historic Commission needed to approve many facets of the project before it could 
move forward. She noted that there was an issue with the HVAC system again with glycol 
leaking, which would likely be expensive to fix. 
Trustee Buckley proposed that the Trustees make a tribute to Miss Selina Little. Trustee Rourke 
volunteered to help. 
Trustee Rourke reported that the Poet Laureate Selection Committee had hosted a public reading 
and recommended a candidate for the new Poet Laureate. Trustee Buckley reported that HSI was 
hosting a Preservation Award ceremony on Tuesday. 
Adjourned 5:29pm.
